questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The natural number 2 is :
questions.solution: 2 has exactly two factors, 1 and itself, so it is prime (the only even prime).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: For any natural number n, 6ⁿ ends with the digit :
questions.solution: 6 × 6 = 36 ends in 6, and multiplying any number ending in 6 by 6 again ends in 6. So 6ⁿ always ends in 6.

questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If a pair of linear equations in two variables is represented by two coincident lines, then the pair of equations has :
questions.solution: Coincident lines share every point, so there are infinitely many solutions.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If Δ ABC and Δ DEF are similar such that 2 AB = DE and BC = 8 cm, then EF is equal to :
questions.solution: DE/AB = 2, so every side of Δ DEF is twice the matching side of Δ ABC. EF = 2 × BC = 16 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The mid-point of the line segment joining the points (5, −4) and (6, 4) lies on :
questions.solution: Mid-point = (11/2, 0). Its y-coordinate is 0, so it lies on the x-axis.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Given that sin θ = a/b, then cos θ is equal to :
questions.solution: Take opposite side a and hypotenuse b; the adjacent side is √(b² − a²). So cos θ = √(b² − a²)/b.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If TP and TQ are two tangents to a circle with centre O from an external point T so that ∠POQ = 120°, then ∠PTQ is equal to :
questions.solution: In quadrilateral OPTQ, the angles at P and Q are 90°. So ∠PTQ = 360° − 90° − 90° − 120° = 60°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The hour hand of a clock is 7 cm long. The angle swept by it between 7:00 a.m. and 8:10 a.m. is :
questions.solution: The hour hand turns 30° per hour, i.e. 0.5° per minute. From 7:00 to 8:10 is 70 minutes, so it sweeps 70 × 0.5° = 35°.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of diameter '2d' is :
questions.solution: The radius is d. Total surface area of a solid hemisphere = 3πr² = 3πd².

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the mean and mode of a data are 12 and 21 respectively, then its median is :
questions.solution: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean: 21 = 3 Median − 24, so Median = 15.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A die is thrown once. Probability of getting a number other than 3 is :
questions.solution: 5 of the 6 outcomes are not 3, so P = 5/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The probability that a leap year has 53 Mondays is 2/7.
Reason (R): The probability that a non-leap year has 53 Mondays is 5/7.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: A leap year has 52 weeks and 2 extra days; 2 of the 7 possible pairs include a Monday, so A is true. A non-leap year has 1 extra day, so the probability is 1/7, not 5/7. R is false.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The polynomial p(y) = y² + 4y + 3 has two zeroes.
Reason (R): A quadratic polynomial can have at most two zeroes.
options: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: y² + 4y + 3 = (y + 1)(y + 3), with zeroes −1 and −3, so A is true. R is true, but 'at most two' does not explain why this polynomial has exactly two zeroes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If α, β are the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = x² − 3x − 1, then find the value of 1/α + 1/β.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In Δ ABC, DE ∥ BC. If AD = x, DB = x − 2, AE = x + 2 and EC = x − 1, then find the value of x.
questions.solution: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, AD/DB = AE/EC: x/(x − 2) = (x + 2)/(x − 1). So x(x − 1) = (x + 2)(x − 2), i.e. x² − x = x² − 4, and x = 4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The coordinates of the centre of a circle are (x − 7, 2x). Find the value(s) of 'x', if the circle passes through the point (−9, 11) and has radius 5√2 units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If tan θ = 24/7, then find the value of sin θ + cos θ.
questions.solution: Take opposite side 24 and adjacent side 7; hypotenuse = √(576 + 49) = 25. sin θ = 24/25 and cos θ = 7/25, so sin θ + cos θ = 31/25.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If cot θ = 7/8, then find the value of ((1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ)) / ((1 + cos θ)(1 − cos θ)).
questions.solution: The expression is (1 − sin²θ)/(1 − cos²θ) = cos²θ/sin²θ = cot²θ = 49/64.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two concentric circles are of radii 5 cm and 4 cm. Find the length of the chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle.
questions.solution: The radius of the smaller circle to the point of contact is perpendicular to the chord and bisects it. Half the chord = √(5² − 4²) = 3 cm, so the chord is 6 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that √3 is an irrational number.
questions.solution: Assume √3 = a/b with a, b coprime integers, b ≠ 0. Then a² = 3b², so 3 divides a², hence 3 divides a. Write a = 3c: 9c² = 3b², so b² = 3c² and 3 divides b. Then 3 divides both a and b, contradicting that they are coprime. So √3 is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the ratio in which the x-axis divides the line segment joining the points (−6, 5) and (−4, −1). Also, find the point of intersection.
questions.solution: Let the ratio be k : 1. On the x-axis y = 0, so (−k + 5)/(k + 1) = 0 and k = 5. The ratio is 5 : 1. x = (5 × (−4) + 1 × (−6))/6 = −26/6 = −13/3. The point is (−13/3, 0).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If x = h + a cos θ, y = k + b sin θ, then prove that : ((x − h)/a)² + ((y − k)/b)² = 1
questions.solution: (x − h)/a = cos θ and (y − k)/b = sin θ. So the left side is cos²θ + sin²θ = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Prove that : tan A/(1 + sec A) − tan A/(1 − sec A) = 2 cosec A
questions.solution: LHS = tan A [(1 − sec A) − (1 + sec A)] / (1 − sec²A) = tan A (−2 sec A)/(−tan²A) = 2 sec A/tan A = 2 × (1/cos A) × (cos A/sin A) = 2/sin A = 2 cosec A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Δ ABC is a right triangle in which ∠B = 90°, AB = 4 cm and BC = 3 cm. Find the radius of the circle inscribed in the triangle ABC.
questions.solution: AC = √(4² + 3²) = 5 cm. Let the radius be r. The tangent lengths from B are both r, so from A they are 4 − r and from C they are 3 − r, and AC = (4 − r) + (3 − r) = 5. So 7 − 2r = 5 and r = 1 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A circle touches the side QR of Δ PQR at S and extended sides PQ and PR at M and N respectively. Prove that : PM = ½ (PQ + QR + PR)
questions.solution: Tangents from an external point are equal: PM = PN, QM = QS and RN = RS. So PQ + QR + PR = PQ + QS + SR + PR = PQ + QM + RN + PR = PM + PN = 2PM. Hence PM = ½ (PQ + QR + PR).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A solid is in the form of a cylinder with hemispherical ends. The total height of the solid is 20 cm and the diameter of the cylinder is 7 cm. Find the total volume of the solid. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution: r = 3.5 cm and the cylinder's height is 20 − 7 = 13 cm. Cylinder: πr²h = (22/7) × 12.25 × 13 = 500.5 cm³. Two hemispheres make a sphere: (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 42.875 = 539/3 ≈ 179.67 cm³. Total ≈ 680.17 cm³ (exactly 4081/6 cm³).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two dice of different colours are thrown at the same time. Write down all the possible outcomes. What is the probability that : (i) same number appears on both the dice ? (ii) different number appears on both the dice ?
questions.solution: The outcomes are the 36 ordered pairs (1, 1), (1, 2), …, (1, 6), (2, 1), …, (6, 6). (i) Same number: (1, 1), (2, 2), …, (6, 6), which is 6 outcomes, so P = 6/36 = 1/6. (ii) Different numbers: P = 1 − 1/6 = 5/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
questions.text: Determine graphically, the coordinates of vertices of a triangle whose equations are 2x − 3y + 6 = 0; 2x + 3y − 18 = 0 and x = 0. Also, find the area of this triangle.
questions.solution: Plot the lines. 2x − 3y + 6 = 0 passes through (0, 2) and (3, 4). 2x + 3y − 18 = 0 passes through (0, 6) and (3, 4). x = 0 is the y-axis. The vertices are (0, 2), (0, 6) and (3, 4). Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × (6 − 2) × 3 = 6 square units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A faster train takes one hour less than a slower train for a journey of 200 km. If the speed of the slower train is 10 km/hr less than that of the faster train, find the speeds of the two trains.
questions.solution: Let the faster train's speed be v km/h, so the slower one's is v − 10. 200/(v − 10) − 200/v = 1 gives 2000 = v(v − 10), i.e. v² − 10v − 2000 = 0. This factorises as (v − 50)(v + 40) = 0, so v = 50. The speeds are 50 km/h and 40 km/h.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum of the areas of two squares is 640 m². If the difference in their perimeters is 64 m, find the sides of the two squares.
questions.solution: Let the sides be a and b with a > b. 4a − 4b = 64 gives a = b + 16. Then (b + 16)² + b² = 640, so 2b² + 32b − 384 = 0, i.e. b² + 16b − 192 = 0. This factorises as (b + 24)(b − 8) = 0, so b = 8 and a = 24. The sides are 24 m and 8 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: State and prove Basic Proportionality Theorem.
questions.solution: Statement: if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio. Proof: let DE ∥ BC in ΔABC, with D on AB and E on AC. Join BE and CD, and draw EN ⊥ AB and DM ⊥ AC. ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = AD/DB and ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = AE/EC. ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels, so their areas are equal. Hence AD/DB = AE/EC.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: CM and RN are respectively the medians of Δ ABC and Δ PQR. If Δ ABC ~ Δ PQR, then prove that : (i) Δ AMC ~ Δ PNR (ii) Δ CMB ~ Δ RNQ
questions.solution: Since Δ ABC ~ Δ PQR: ∠A = ∠P, ∠B = ∠Q and AB/PQ = BC/QR = CA/RP. (i) AM = AB/2 and PN = PQ/2, so AM/PN = AB/PQ = CA/RP. With ∠A = ∠P, Δ AMC ~ Δ PNR (SAS). (ii) MB = AB/2 and NQ = PQ/2, so MB/NQ = AB/PQ = BC/QR. With ∠B = ∠Q, Δ CMB ~ Δ RNQ (SAS).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In a potato race, a bucket is placed at the starting point, which is 5 m from the first potato. The other potatoes are arranged 3 m apart in a straight line, with a total of 10 potatoes. A competitor starts from the bucket, picks up the nearest potato, runs back to the bucket to drop it in, then returns to pick up the next potato. This process continues until all the potatoes are in the bucket.

What is the distance covered to pick up the first potato and drop it in bucket ?
questions.solution: 5 m there and 5 m back: 10 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In a potato race, a bucket is placed at the starting point, which is 5 m from the first potato. The other potatoes are arranged 3 m apart in a straight line, with a total of 10 potatoes. A competitor starts from the bucket, picks up the nearest potato, runs back to the bucket to drop it in, then returns to pick up the next potato. This process continues until all the potatoes are in the bucket.

What is the distance covered to pick up the second potato and drop it in bucket ?
questions.solution: The second potato is 5 + 3 = 8 m away, so 8 m there and 8 m back: 16 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In a potato race, a bucket is placed at the starting point, which is 5 m from the first potato. The other potatoes are arranged 3 m apart in a straight line, with a total of 10 potatoes. A competitor starts from the bucket, picks up the nearest potato, runs back to the bucket to drop it in, then returns to pick up the next potato. This process continues until all the potatoes are in the bucket.

What is the total distance the competitor has to run ?
questions.solution: The round trips are 10, 16, 22, … m, an AP with a = 10, d = 6 and 10 terms. S₁₀ = (10/2)(2 × 10 + 9 × 6) = 5 × 74 = 370 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
In a potato race, a bucket is placed at the starting point, which is 5 m from the first potato. The other potatoes are arranged 3 m apart in a straight line, with a total of 10 potatoes. A competitor starts from the bucket, picks up the nearest potato, runs back to the bucket to drop it in, then returns to pick up the next potato. This process continues until all the potatoes are in the bucket.

If average speed of competitor is 5 m/s, then find the average time taken by competitor to put all the potatoes in the bucket.
questions.solution: Total distance = 10 + 16 + … (10 terms) = 370 m. Time = 370 ÷ 5 = 74 seconds.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A radio station tower was built in two sections 'A' and 'B'. Tower is supported by wires from a point 'O'. Distance between the base of the tower and point 'O' is 6 m. From point 'O', the angle of elevation of the top of the section 'B' is 30° and the angle of elevation of the top of section 'A' is 60°.

Find the distance AB.
questions.solution: Height to the top of A = 6 tan 60° = 6√3 m. Height to the top of B = 6 tan 30° = 2√3 m. AB = 6√3 − 2√3 = 4√3 m.

questions.text:
A brooch is crafted from silver wire in the shape of a circle with a diameter of 35 cm. The wire is also used to create 5 diameters, dividing the circle into 10 equal sectors.

What is the radius of circle ?
questions.solution: Radius = 35 ÷ 2 = 17.5 cm.
